_: Life at the working buildings (works.gd, town_life.gd, npc_mind.gd, villagers.gd; docs/TUNING.md). The town agent places each trade's building and lists it on the town's root as meta works: {trade: {at, yaw, spots: {name: Vector3}, node, component}} (town-local; yaw turns the building's front, +z, out to the street). A building listed with no spots takes its component's work spots from assets.json (components.<component>.work) or, failing that, the defaults here (spots: metres from the building's middle, x along its front, z out of it, y up). aliases: other names the town data may use. fallback: where a trade's work goes when the town lacks it (a town with no bakery bakes at its granary). Off with --works=off.
_paddock: paddock: how far the horses roam from its middle (metres) when the town agent gives no fence; amble: their walking pace (world units a second; a horse walks at 0.2); rest: seconds each stands between strolls (fewest, most); follow: how far behind the groom a led horse walks (world units); tied_secs: how long a horse waits tied at the inn before it is taken home on its own; lead_most: seconds a horse is led before it is let go whatever happened to its groom. A town with stables but no paddock grazes its horses round the stables' middle spot.
_counts: How many work at each building, by the town's state: base, then the first state in priority that the town is in (a feast beats war at the inn). States: hunger and feast (the town's mood), levy (a muster at the town this season or last), war (its house at war), justice, relief, grant, build (a court ruling standing at the town: the bridge's rulings.js; a feast or levy ruled is that state), low (its granary under a quarter full), prosperity. size_per adds one per that many of the town's size; most caps it.
_jobs: Townsfolk out and about given a trade when their town has its building (villagers.gd): how many of each. apprentice (forge: bellows, quench, coal, arms to the armoury), groom (stables: horses led to the inn and the gate, fodder, mucking out), carter (the grain chain: field to mill, mill to granary, bread to the market).
_weights: How a town's state shifts the odds of what people at the buildings choose next (npc_mind.gd Weigh), multiplied in. Keys are activity names.
_forge: The forge's look: glow (its light's colour, energy by day at work, by night banked, and in war or a levy; range in world units; inset: how far inside the hearth it sits, from the hearth's mouth toward the building), sparks off the anvil, a burst each hammer stroke (how many, how long each lives, how fast they fly, their size in world units, how high over the anvil's foot, how bright at most: they're added, so 1 blooms; war multiplies the amount).
_mill: Mills turn while they work (by day, and with grain in the town): spin_names (the parts of a mill model that turn, by name), axis per kind (the part's own axis), rpm at full work, and how fast it comes up to speed or runs down (a share a second).
_inn: The inn at night: its windows lit (light colour, energy from dusk, range in world units); the bench drinkers go in at night. By day: tables, long tables in its yard, seats a side (batch 7: no tables at the inn; the crown's men at the first in war or a levy).
_day: The working day by the village clock (hours): when the forge and mill work, when the inn's benches fill, when the windows are lit.
_yard: The barn's yard: the town's beasts in a loose pen round the barn's yard spot (counts.beasts; a war takes some for the host, hunger eats them): kinds, each [kind, how often it's picked] (a kind with no model in this build is skipped); roam: how far from the yard spot they stand (metres); gap: the least room between two beasts, or a beast and a person (metres). Each lives its own idle life (animals.json). counts.yardhands: who tends them (npc_mind post yardhand: milking, feeding, the trough, mucking out). counts.inn_soldiers: the crown's men who take the inn's benches first in war or a levy.
_crier: The crier in the square when there's news (war, a levy, a feast, hunger, a low granary): how far from the well he stands (world units) and how far round him his listeners stand.
_stock: What lies stacked at the buildings: swords on the armoury rack (most, at the start), sacks by the mill (most, at the start), and sacks by the granary (most: its pile shows how full Freeciv says the granary is).
